title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 204 (Secretarial audit for bigger companies)

content.overview: Section 204 requires every listed company and every other company belonging to such class or classes as may be prescribed to annex with its Board’s report a secretarial audit report, given by a company secretary in practice, in such form as may be prescribed. The report states whether the company has complied with the provisions of the Act, rules, regulations and secretarial standards, and any other law as may be prescribed. The Board must explain in full any qualification or observation in the report. It is not a substitute for the statutory financial audit.
content.glance: Listed companies and prescribed classes: annex secretarial audit report by a company secretary in practice to the Board’s report; compliance with Act, rules, regulations and secretarial standards; Board explains qualifications; not a financial audit.
content.study: Every listed company and a company belonging to such other class of companies as may be prescribed shall annex with its Board’s report made under section 134, a secretarial audit report, given by a company secretary in practice, in such form as may be prescribed. It shall be the duty of the company to give all assistance and facilities to the company secretary in practice, for auditing the secretarial and related records. The Board of Directors, in their report, shall explain in full any qualification or observation or other remarks made by the company secretary in practice. Current-law framing: confirm listed or prescribed class; ensure secretarial audit by a CS in practice; annex report to Board’s report under s. 134; Board explains any qualification. Distinct from statutory financial audit under Chapter X.

sections.heading: Applicability
sections.body: Every listed company and every other company of a prescribed class must obtain and annex a secretarial audit report.

sections.heading: Auditor and Form
sections.body: Report given by a company secretary in practice, in the prescribed form.

sections.heading: Content and Board Response
sections.body: Report addresses compliance with the Act, rules, regulations and secretarial standards (and other prescribed law). Board explains any qualification or observation in full in its report.

sections.heading: Assistance
sections.body: Company must give all assistance and facilities to the CS in practice for auditing secretarial and related records.

examples.title: Listed company without secretarial audit
examples.body: A listed company files its Board’s report under s. 134 without annexing a secretarial audit report from a company secretary in practice. Section 204 is breached.

examples.title: Qualification not explained
examples.body: The secretarial auditor qualifies the report for non-compliance with a secretarial standard. The Board’s report does not explain the qualification. Section 204 requires the Board to explain any qualification in full.

hypotheticals.question: Does a clean financial audit under Chapter X dispense with secretarial audit under s. 204?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Secretarial audit is a separate compliance audit by a company secretary in practice for listed and prescribed companies. It is not a substitute for, and is not replaced by, the statutory financial audit.

distinctions.title: Secretarial audit (s. 204) vs statutory financial audit (Chapter X)
distinctions.left: Compliance with Act, rules, regulations and secretarial standards by a CS in practice
distinctions.right: True and fair view of financial statements by a chartered accountant

misconceptions.trap: Only listed companies need secretarial audit; no other class is covered.
misconceptions.correction: Section 204 applies to every listed company and every other company belonging to such class or classes as may be prescribed.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 204 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm listed or prescribed class. II. Check CS-in-practice report annexed to Board’s report. III. Test Board explanation of qualifications. IV. Distinguish financial audit. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Applicability; report status; Board explanation; precise relief.

examTips: Not a substitute for financial audit.
